habitat: Thickets in coastal bush, forest, riverine forest and valley bush. It stays in dense cover and raises its tail often.
summary: A common resident. Entirely orange from above the eyes and the sides of the head to the undertail, with no white eyebrow. The immature is spotted. The call is a repeated double note, and the song includes whistled phrases and imitations. The Kemp name Natal Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Orange from above the eyes and the sides of the head. No white eyebrow.

viewNotes.note: Orange head and underparts, with no white eyebrow.

calls.description: A monotonous double note, 'trrree-trrirr', continued for long periods. The song is whistled phrases and imitations. The grade A call is from St Lucia. The filename is XC349556-2016-11-28 St Lucia Gwalagwala - Red-capped Robin Chat (Natal Robin).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A call is from KwaZulu-Natal. The Kemp name Natal Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^12=4096 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 2048–8192.
